::: {#sol-pairs-with-repetition}

There are $\frac{N(N + 1)}{2}$ choices, which is $\binomial{N + 1}{2}$.

As in @sol-toppings,
each choice is a set $\set{a, b}$ with $a, b \in S$,
and the set has one of two forms.

- **Two different elements.**
  These are the $2$-element subsets of $S$,
  and there are $\binomial{N}{2} = \frac{N(N - 1)}{2}$ of them by @thm-binomial-two.
- **The same element twice.**
  These are the sets $\set{a}$ with $a \in S$,
  and there are $N$ of them.

Adding the two counts, one operation per line:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{N(N - 1)}{2} + N
&= \frac{N(N - 1)}{2} + \frac{2N}{2}
&& \text{writing } N = \tfrac{2N}{2} \\
&= \frac{N(N - 1) + 2N}{2}
&& \text{adding fractions with the same denominator} \\
&= \frac{N^2 - N + 2N}{2}
&& \text{distributing } N \\
&= \frac{N^2 + N}{2}
&& \text{combining } -N + 2N \\
&= \frac{N(N + 1)}{2}
&& \text{factoring out } N \\
&= \binomial{N + 1}{2}
&& \text{taking } n = N + 1 \text{ in the theorem}
\end{aligned}
$$

The last line applies @thm-binomial-two with $n = N + 1$.
For the five toppings, $N = 5$ gives $\frac{5 \cdot 6}{2} = 15$ choices, as in @sol-toppings.

:::
